paper_title: Constraints on hidden photons produced in nuclear reactors
coupling_convention: kinetic mixing epsilon, dimensionless (plot axis is Log10 epsilon; emitted values are linear epsilon)
notes: Paper reanalyzes published TEXONO reactor neutrino data to set a revised 95% CL limit on hidden-photon kinetic mixing epsilon vs mass mX, including photon-hidden-photon oscillations in matter. Main result is Fig. 1 (black solid TEXONO line), for which no numerical table is given. Data points are reconstructed from text: for mX >~ 20 eV the limit is stated to be only slightly weaker (factor 4 in signal, epsilon^4 dependence => ~4^{1/4}~1.4x) than Park's epsilon ~ 1e-5, giving epsilon ~ 1.4e-5 flat up to the kinematic limit ~1 MeV. Below the effective photon mass mgamma ~ 20 eV the signal scales as epsilon^4 (mX/mgamma)^8, so limit scales as (mgamma/mX)^2, becoming insensitive (epsilon~1) below ~0.1 eV, as the paper states. Points are approximate; treat coupling values below 20 eV with caution. Not a DM haloscope, so no local DM density assumption. Resonance region (mX ~ mgamma) enhancement not included in curve. | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0.85, 36)) | Vision: Fig. 1 shows the 95% CL upper limit on kinetic mixing epsilon vs hidden photon mass from TEXONO reactor data (black solid line), the paper's main result. Axes are Log10(m_X/eV) from -2 to 6 and Log10(epsilon) from 0 to -15. The boundary is a diagonal with slope -2 (epsilon ~ m^-2) from m~0.13 eV (epsilon~1) to the kink at m~20 eV (the assumed effective photon mass m_gamma~20 eV), then a mass-independent plateau at epsilon ~ 4e-5 up to 1e6 eV. Below m~0.13 eV there is no constraint (epsilon>1). Other shaded regions (CAST, Solar Lifetime, HB, Rydberg, dDM, EW) are prior constraints, not traced.
